Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Situation2: Medical advice suggests this may be their final opportunity to travel long distances.
Story:
It was 2 a.m. when my phone buzzed, jolting me awake. My best friend’s name flashed on the screen, and I answered to the sound of her sobs. She could barely speak, but I understood enough—her father had just passed away unexpectedly. She needed me, she said, just to listen, to be there, to help her hold the pieces together. I sat up, heart pounding, trying to offer comfort through the phone, feeling her pain as if it were my own.

But as I listened, my mind kept drifting to the plane ticket on my desk. Tomorrow, I was supposed to leave for Hajj. The doctor had been clear: my health was declining, and this might be my last chance to fulfill this pillar of my faith. I had waited years for this moment, saved every penny, and prayed for the opportunity. Now, my friend needed me more than ever, but so did my faith. The weight of both expectations pressed down on me, and I felt torn in two, unable to imagine how I could possibly choose between them.
